name: severity
summary: The severity INDICATOR — a coloured dot (+ optional label + tooltip) for a severity LEVEL (down / critical / major / warning / clear / up / maintenance / unreachable / unknown / …). Distinct from MStatusTag, which maps status STRINGS to tag-* pills. Used 80×. Renders --severity-<level>; can take `severity` directly or resolve it live from a monitor (objectId / instance / counter) via DB workers.

variants.name: solid-chip
variants.what: filled pill: background --severity-<level> + white text (the plain mode)

variants.name: text
variants.what: coloured numeric/value text in --severity-<level>, JetBrains Mono (.text mode)

variants.name: stripe
variants.what: severity-stripe.vue — coloured left rule on a list row/card

states.name: live
states.what: resolves from objectId / instance / counter via severityDBWorker + the live EVENT_SEVERITY_COUNTER_DB_CHANGED bus event

severityLevels.$note: each level -> --severity-<level> (the dot/text colour) + --severity-<level>-dot-box (the halo). Resolve via tokens/variables.json. QUIRK (mirrored from severity.less): `up` = green ring (--severity-clear) + a critical/light-red centre (--severity-critical-dot-box); `down`/`disable` have no -dot-box (down renders solid).

props.objectId: [Number,String] — monitor id / name / IP to live-resolve from the DB worker
props.displayText: Boolean (false) — show the Capitalize(severity) label beside the dot

events.udpate:severity: (sic — misspelled in source) the resolved level after live lookup

decisionFlow: Showing a monitor/alert SEVERITY level (critical/major/warning/clear/up/down/…)? -> Severity (dot).
Showing a STATUS string (up/down/running/failed/poweredoff…) as a pill? -> MStatusTag (Tag family).
Need a coloured stripe down a list row/card? -> severity-stripe.
Let the user pick a severity level (policy/condition forms)? -> severity-picker.
Show counts per severity on a dashboard? -> severity-count-box.
do: Use Severity for severity LEVELS; MStatusTag for status STRINGS.
Pass `severity` directly when you already have it; use objectId/instance/counter only for live resolution.
Resolve colours via --severity-<level> (+ --severity-<level>-dot-box for the halo).
dont: Don't route alert/monitor severity through MStatusTag — its TAG_MAP lacks major/warning/clear, so they render as a grey plain tag (F7).
Don't hardcode severity colours — use the --severity-* tokens.
Don't rely on the dot colour alone for a11y — set displayText or keep the tooltip.

F1.issue: emit name is misspelled `udpate:severity` in source.

F2.issue: colour-dot only by default — set displayText / keep the tooltip so severity isn't colour-only (WCAG 1.4.1).

renderShapesNote: The same severity.less class set renders dot / solid-chip / text / bg-fill (mode = a class on the element). Severity is ALSO shown via the chart/graph layer using the same --severity-* tokens: topology graph-node colour, RUM apdex map markers, heatmap cells, availability segments (see data-viz-tooltips / table) — cross-referenced, not duplicated.

a11y.summary: Must NOT be colour-only (F2) — pair the dot with a label (displayText) or keep the tooltip; announce live changes meaningfully.
a11y.$note: Catalogue-wide gap SF-001 = no visible :focus-visible ring; tracked in findings/.

slots: none — presentational (renders the dot + optional label from props; no slots)
changelog: 2026-06-27: added to the Elements site — 13 severity levels in dot / dot+label / solid-chip / coloured-text / bg-fill shapes; source-accurate 11px dot (the Storybook reproduction enlarges to 14px).
2026-06-29: stripe shown in both real usages — the standalone bar AND the table/list left-rule row.

dot.useWhen: Default. You have a monitor/alert severity LEVEL (critical/major/warning/clear/up/down/maintenance/…) and need the compact colour indicator in a dense context — a grid cell, list row, topology node, or inline beside a name — where a coloured dot plus hover tooltip conveys the level without eating horizontal space. Pass `severity` directly, or `objectId`(+`instance`/`counter`) to live-resolve.
dot.dontUse: Don't use in an a11y-sensitive standalone context where the dot is the only signal (WCAG 1.4.1, F2) — add `displayText` (dot+label) or keep the tooltip. For a status STRING (running/failed/poweredoff) use MStatusTag, not this. For counts per level use count-box; for a left row rule use stripe.
dot.example: The severity dot beside each monitor in the Inventory monitor list and on topology graph nodes, resolving live from the monitor's objectId via the DB worker.

dot+label.useWhen: You want the dot AND the capitalized level text — set `displayText=true`. Preferred for accessibility (satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 so severity isn't colour-only) and for standalone contexts with room for a word: detail panels, alert headers, cards where the reader shouldn't have to hover to learn the level.
dot+label.dontUse: Don't use in tight grid cells or icon rails where the label wraps or crowds the layout — use the bare `dot` (with tooltip) there. Don't use for choosing a level (that's picker) or for aggregate counts (count-box).
dot+label.example: The alert detail header showing the dot followed by 'Critical' / 'Major', so the level reads without hovering.

solid-chip.useWhen: You need a filled pill — background `--severity-<level>` with white text (the plain/solid mode) — for a high-emphasis, standalone severity badge that must stand out on its own, e.g. a prominent alert-severity badge in a header or banner where a small dot would be too subtle.
solid-chip.dontUse: Don't use in dense tables/lists where a filled pill per row is visually heavy — use `dot`. Don't confuse with MStatusTag's `tag-*` pills: those map status STRINGS; solid-chip is still the Severity component rendering a severity LEVEL. Don't hardcode the fill — use `--severity-<level>`.
solid-chip.example: A filled critical/major severity badge in an alert banner or summary header, using the --severity-<level> background with white text.

text.useWhen: You have a numeric or value string that should be tinted by severity — coloured `--severity-<level>` text in JetBrains Mono (`.text` mode). Use for metric values, thresholds, or counts whose colour must communicate the level while keeping the number readable, e.g. a monitored value shown in critical red.
text.dontUse: Don't use for a categorical level indicator where a dot reads faster (`dot`/`dot+label`). Don't rely on colour alone for the number's meaning if the value must be understood by colour-blind users — pair with a label. Don't hardcode the colour; use the `--severity-<level>` token.
text.example: A KPI/threshold metric value rendered in --severity-critical red monospaced text when it breaches the critical threshold.

bg-fill.useWhen: You need to tint a whole row or cell by severity — `--severity-<level>-lighter` background tint + 1px `--severity-<level>` border (generateSeverityBg / `.bg`). Use to make an entire alert/monitor row scannable by severity at a glance in a grid or list.
bg-fill.dontUse: Don't use when only the indicator needs colour (use `dot`) or when a left edge rule suffices (use `stripe`) — a full-cell tint is heavier. Avoid on already-dense tables where the tint fights other status colours. Don't hardcode; use the `-lighter` + border tokens.
bg-fill.example: An alert grid where each critical/major row is tinted with the matching --severity-<level>-lighter background so operators triage by scanning colour.

stripe.useWhen: You want a coloured left rule down a list row or card (`severity-stripe.vue`) to band items by severity without tinting the whole surface. Per the decisionFlow: 'Need a coloured stripe down a list row/card? → severity-stripe.' Shown both as a standalone bar and as a table/list left-rule row.
stripe.dontUse: Don't use when the full row should be tinted (that's bg-fill) or when a compact inline mark is enough (dot). Don't use to pick a level (picker) or to show counts (count-box).
stripe.example: The coloured left-edge rule on each alert/notification list row (and the standalone severity bar), banding rows by --severity-<level>.

picker.useWhen: You need to let the USER choose a severity level — `severity-picker.vue` / `compliance-severity-picker`. Per the decisionFlow: 'Let the user pick a severity level (policy/condition forms)? → severity-picker.' Use in alert-policy and condition/threshold forms where an author sets which level a rule maps to.
picker.dontUse: Don't use to merely DISPLAY a resolved level (use `dot`/`dot+label`). Don't hand-roll a level dropdown — the picker already renders the --severity-* swatches.
picker.example: The severity selector in an alert-policy / threshold-condition form (and compliance-severity-picker in compliance rules) where the author assigns critical/major/warning to a condition.

count-box.useWhen: You need to show COUNTS per severity on a dashboard — `dashboard/severity-count-box.vue`. Per the decisionFlow: 'Show counts per severity on a dashboard? → severity-count-box.' Use for the at-a-glance tally of how many objects sit at each level.
count-box.dontUse: Don't use for a single object's level (that's `dot`/`dot+label`) or to pick a level (picker). Don't rebuild an aggregate tile from bare dots — count-box already pairs each --severity-<level> with its number.
count-box.example: The dashboard summary box tallying counts of critical / major / warning / clear monitors across the environment.

switch.useWhen: You need an alert-severity TOGGLE control (severity-switch) — a switch-style control for enabling/setting severity, catalogued under Atoms/Radio. Use where a form toggles severity handling rather than displaying or free-picking a level.
switch.dontUse: Don't use to display a resolved severity (use `dot`) or to pick from the full list of levels in a form (use `picker`). See Atoms/Radio for the switch's own variants/states — this is a cross-reference, not a distinct Severity render mode.
switch.example: The alert severity toggle (severity-switch) in alert/notification settings, cross-referenced from Atoms/Radio.
